messages:
alex: Heads up - I have a reproducible KV-cache eviction/order bug that only shows up under long-context runs with PagedAttention-style paging. Observed on H100 and A100 but with different failure modes.

alex: Repro steps: run the repro harness in /dev/kv-repro with model ~24B, seq_len=32k, batch=2, continuous sampling. After ~10-20M tokens you start seeing token corruption and memory growth.

alex: Minimal repro snippet I used (python):

```
# alloc pages, stream many forward passes, trigger evict
for i in range(100_000):
    ctx = model.forward(stream_input(i))
    # touch different kv slots, force page table churn
    kv.touch_pages(ctx.kv, pattern=i % 4096)
```

alex: On H100 behaviour: memory usage climbs slowly, page-table entries get reused (slot x -> slot y) but KV contents sometimes point to previous page's buffer -> gibberish tokens. Non-deterministic, shows up after many reuses.

alex: On A100 behaviour: occasionally we get CUDA memory OOMs when eviction should have freed pages (evict callbacks not firing), then a cascade of retries in the runtime leading to long stalls.

maya: :eyes: can you paste the small pte dump and a runtime log where it fails? Also which drivers? NVIDIA driver 535.86 on H100 here.

alex: Dump (pte_index:owner,page_id):

```
# before run
0x1f4:owner=slot_1024,page=0x7f3a
0x1f5:owner=slot_1025,page=0x7f4b
...
# after reuse
0x1f4:owner=slot_2048,page=0x7f4b  # page pointer moved but owner idx stayed
0x1f5:owner=slot_1026,page=0x7f3a  # swapped unexpectedly
```

alex: Runtime log snippet (abridged):

```
[evict] candidate_page=0x7f3a refcnt=0 -> queued
[alloc] new_page=0x7f4b assigned to slot_2048
[pt-update] idx=0x1f4 <- page=0x7f4b
[gc] freed page=0x7f3a
[decode] found kv ptr=0x7f3a (expected 0x7f4b) -> token_mismatch
```

ryan: Huh. That looks like an ordering/race in the page-table update vs free path. Are we draining device streams correctly before reassigning pages? Could be different stream semantics on H100 vs A100.

chen: I ran the repro on A100 with driver 525.x and I saw evict callbacks missing too. My hypothesis: our host-side free queue is processed on a dedicated worker thread that uses cudaStreamSynchronize(stream) on the worker stream, but sometimes we post frees across multiple streams without proper memfence ordering. Different GPU architectures have different completion timings so it becomes data-racey.

maya: Did you try forcing a cudaDeviceSynchronize() before pt-update as a debug check? That'll be slow but helps isolate ordering.

alex: I added a debug sync and the corruption stops, but throughput drops 3x. So ordering is likely the root cause. However, the A100 OOMs still happen occasionally even with sync - suggests we also have a leak in the sparse free-list path.

alex: Perf counters from the repro (approx):

```
H100: stall_cycles +18%, L2_miss +35%, page_faults +0.4%
A100: stall_cycles +9%, L2_miss +12%, driver_retries +200%
```

alex: Note the higher L2 miss and stall on H100 - maybe the reuse pattern is causing bad locality and exposing a bug in our allocator's tiling assumptions.

ryan: Could this be related to our page-table tiling optimization (we tile PTEs per-SM for locality)? If the driver remaps or reorders pages at free time we might be assuming stable physical layout.

chen: Also seen a mismatch in our PT page size config vs CUDA default on certain OS builds (4KB vs 64KB granularity). If our PTE indexing math assumes 64KB pages but driver uses 4KB, index collisions could happen.

maya: Ok next steps proposed:
- alex: attach the full repro script and a small trace (nvprof / Nsight) capture
- chen: add assert+sync on free path to ensure ordering and run full nightly on both H100/A100 images
- ryan: look at tiling code: add a fallback path that avoids per-SM PTE striping (simpler linear PTE map) and run quick perf/regression

maya: Also add a runtime flag KVCACHE_DBG_FORCE_SYNC to flip syncs for canary runs in CI.

alex: I'll upload repro + capture to the thread: https://internal/redwood/dev/kv-repro/1839991234

infra-bot: Scheduled nightly job kv-repro-h100 at 02:00 UTC with KVCACHE_DBG_FORCE_SYNC=false

ryan: If the forced sync removes the bug, we can try to replace full device sync with stream-ordered release + memory barriers. Full device sync is too expensive.

chen: I will instrument the free queue to tag each freed page with epoch and assert pt->owner_epoch == freed_epoch before reuse to detect misordered reuse.

maya: Good plan. If you want, I can take the A100 nightly and spin that consumer loop under driver 525 vs 535 to see driver sensitivity.

alex: Thanks. Also we should consider a temporary mitigation: keep one guard page per allocation that we never reuse (to detect stale pointer use) - cheap way to detect corrupted read before merge.

alex: TL;DR: reproducible KV page-table eviction/reuse bug triggered under long contexts, shows different symptoms across GPUs (gibberish vs OOM). Likely root causes: stream ordering + page size/tiling assumptions. Next: sync-assert instrumentation + simpler PTE mapping fallback.

maya: :thumbsup: keep updates here and ping if you need help bisecting driver vs runtime code path.
